method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Japanese encephalitis' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anyone aged 2 months and over who lives or works in, or will travel to, a JE risk region of Australia AND may be bitten by mosquitoes.** Risk regions **are determined by states and territories and may change**.
claims.source_text: People aged ≥2 months who live or work in, or are planning travel to, a JE risk region of Australia AND who may be bitten by mosquitoes are recommended to receive JE vaccine Risk regions are determined by states and territories and may change depending on areas in which Japanese encephalitis (JE) virus is detected.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Japanese encephalitis', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/japanese-encephalitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Also: **laboratory workers exposed to JE virus** · **travellers to endemic areas outside Australia in the transmission season** · **people who live or work on the outer islands of Torres Strait**.
claims.source_text: routine vaccination of laboratory workers who may be exposed to JE virus routine vaccination of travellers to endemic areas outside Australia during the JE virus transmission season routine vaccination of people who live or work on the outer islands of Torres Strait
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Japanese encephalitis', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/japanese-encephalitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imojev (live) and JEspect (inactivated) — both safe and effective.** ⚠️ **Imojev is contraindicated in pregnancy and in the immunocompromised, and is not registered under 9 months.** People at ongoing risk **may need boosters**.
claims.source_text: Imojev live JE vaccine and JEspect inactivated JE vaccine. Both vaccines are safe and effective. Imojev is contraindicated in pregnant women and immunocompromised people and is not registered for use in children <9 months of age. People who are at ongoing risk of being infected by JE virus may need booster doses.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Japanese encephalitis', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/japanese-encephalitis, retrieved 2026-09-23
